versions.question: A script must pull just the first 1,048,576 bytes of a large S3 object with `aws s3api get-object`. Which parameter does that?
options: `--max-items 1048576` to cap returned items
`--content-length 1048576` for the response size
`--range bytes=0-1048575` (an HTTP Range)
`--part-number 1` to pick the first segment
versions.explanation: `--range` is sent as an HTTP Range header, so S3 returns only that byte span.

versions.question: Which HTTP request header does the `--range` option of `aws s3api get-object` become on the wire?
options: `If-Match`, a conditional ETag check
`Accept-Ranges`, advertising partial support
The standard `Range` request header
`Content-Range`, the response-side span header
versions.explanation: `--range` maps to the standard `Range` header, and multiple ranged GETs can run in parallel and be stitched together.

versions.question: Before CloudFront VPC origins, a team keeps an internet-facing ALB but wants only CloudFront edges to connect. What is a standard network-level control?
options: Attach an IAM role to the ALB that trusts cloudfront.amazonaws.com as principal
Reference the AWS-managed CloudFront prefix list in the ALB security group's inbound rule
Turn on ALB access logs and have a Lambda block clients whose user agent is not CloudFront's
Release the ALB's public addresses so that its DNS name only resolves inside the VPC
versions.explanation: Public ALBs could be locked down to CloudFront's published IP ranges (prefix list); VPC origins now remove the need for a public ALB.

versions.question: An internet-facing ALB sits behind CloudFront (no VPC origins). Which pair of settings makes the ALB reject direct hits from anyone else?
options: CloudFront signs each origin request with SigV4 and the ALB validates the signature itself
CloudFront adds a secret custom origin header; an ALB rule forwards only requests that carry it
A NACL on the ALB subnet that admits only the CloudFront distribution's ID as source
Route 53 weighted records that send all of the ALB name's lookups to CloudFront only
versions.explanation: A shared-secret header (often combined with the prefix list) was the common pattern before VPC origins.

versions.question: A 1-year TTL is set on `app.js` at CloudFront and each release must reach users instantly, with no invalidation requests. What technique fits?
options: Turn on S3 versioning so CloudFront always reads the newest object version for the same URL
Put a content hash in the file name (like `app.3fa9c1.js`) and have the HTML reference the new name
Add Origin Shield in front of the bucket so edge caches refresh from a single location
Restrict the viewer protocol policy to HTTPS only, which makes edges drop copies cached over HTTP
versions.explanation: A new file name is a new URL and cache key, so nothing needs to be purged.

versions.question: Which statement explains why renaming assets per release avoids CloudFront invalidation costs?
options: Invalidations are free only when the path ends in a version number such as `v2`
Renamed objects skip the cache policy entirely and are always fetched from the origin
A new URL is a different cache key, so old cached copies never need to be removed
CloudFront automatically purges all edge caches whenever an S3 object key changes
versions.explanation: Versioned names sidestep invalidation: old copies just age out unused while viewers request the new URL.

versions.question: Which two are weaknesses of the lazy-loading (cache-aside) pattern? (Choose two)
options: After a database update, the cached copy can stay out of date until it expires or is evicted
Losing one cache node takes the whole application offline until it is manually rebuilt
Database writes are blocked until the cache acknowledges each update synchronously
Only data that has been written by the app in the last minute can be cached
A request for an uncached item needs a cache lookup, a database read and a cache write before it returns
versions.explanation: Misses are slow (three trips) and the cache is only refreshed on reads, so it can serve stale data.

versions.question: Comparing lazy loading with write-through, which two issues belong to lazy loading? (Choose two)
options: The cache may disagree with the database after a direct database change
Each application write has to hit both the cache and the database before completing
The first read of any item pays extra latency because the cache is empty for it
Cache memory is consumed by records nobody ever requests
The cache can never be warmed again after a node replacement
versions.explanation: Write-through avoids stale reads and cold misses but costs extra on writes and can cache unused data; lazy loading has the opposite profile.

versions.question: In Route 53, a parent check should report healthy while at least 2 out of 3 endpoint checks are passing, so one server can be patched without failing DNS. What do you create?
options: A CloudWatch alarm health check tied to a single instance's CPU metric
Three weighted records each with a weight of 33
An endpoint health check with string matching against the response body
A calculated health check that aggregates the three child checks
versions.explanation: Calculated health checks combine child results and let you set how many must pass.

versions.question: What is the maximum number of child health checks a Route 53 calculated health check can monitor?
options: Up to 16 child checks in total
Up to 1,024 child checks, as per zone
Up to 64 child checks per parent
Up to 256 child checks
versions.explanation: A calculated health check can have up to 256 children, with a configurable threshold of how many must be healthy.

versions.question: `api.example.com` has a TTL of 86400 and its IP will change in two days. How do you keep clients from using the old address after cutover?
options: Keep the 24-hour TTL and delete the record at cutover so resolvers forget it at once
Convert the record to a latency-based record, since resolvers ignore the TTL on those records
Change the IP right now since Route 53 pushes changes to every resolver immediately
Cut the TTL to a few minutes now, wait out the old TTL, switch the IP, then restore it
versions.explanation: Resolvers cache for the old TTL, so shorten it ahead of time; low TTL lets changes spread quickly.

versions.question: What is the trade-off of setting a very low TTL on a Route 53 record?
options: The record becomes an alias automatically and loses its health check
Fewer queries are billed, but clients may keep serving stale answers for days after a change
Changes propagate quickly, but resolvers query Route 53 more often, which raises query costs
Records are served faster but can no longer be changed without recreating the hosted zone
versions.explanation: Low TTL means faster changes but more DNS queries (more cost); high TTL is cheaper but slower to update.

versions.question: A script on an AL2023 instance gets HTTP 401 when calling `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`. What must the script do?
options: Call the address `169.254.169.123` instead, which serves metadata on AL2023 hosts
Add a `Host` header that contains the instance ID so the service can route the call
PUT to `/latest/api/token`, then send the returned token in the `X-aws-ec2-metadata-token` header
Attach the `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` managed policy to the instance profile so metadata is authorised
versions.explanation: The instance enforces IMDSv2, which needs a session token.

versions.question: Which instance metadata option makes token-less metadata requests fail with 401 Unauthorized?
options: `HttpPutResponseHopLimit` set to 1
`HttpEndpoint` set to `disabled`
`InstanceMetadataTags` set to `enabled`
`HttpTokens` set to `required`
versions.explanation: With HttpTokens required, only IMDSv2 (token-based) calls succeed.

versions.question: An auditor asks what protects objects in a newly created bucket where nobody configured encryption. What is the answer?
options: Server-side encryption with S3-managed keys using AES-256
Server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key rotated yearly
Client-side encryption performed by the AWS Encryption SDK before upload
Nothing, objects stay in plaintext until a bucket policy requires encryption
versions.explanation: SSE-S3 is applied to all new objects by default.

versions.question: An object was uploaded with no encryption headers to a new bucket. Which value will `x-amz-server-side-encryption` show on a HEAD request?
options: `aws:kms:dsse`, dual-layer KMS encryption
`aws:kms` with the aws/s3 managed key
`SSE-C`, supplied by the client
The value `AES256`, meaning SSE-S3
versions.explanation: Default encryption is SSE-S3, reported as AES256.

versions.question: Clients far from the Region upload multi-GB files slowly. Which two techniques speed up the upload? (Choose two)
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration through the nearest edge location
Spreading key names across more prefixes
Multipart upload with parts sent in parallel
Moving the objects to Standard-IA after upload
Byte-range GET requests issued in parallel
versions.explanation: Multipart and Transfer Acceleration help uploads; ranged GETs help downloads.

versions.question: A 20 GB object must be downloaded faster. Which approach helps most?
options: Transition the object to Standard-IA so reads use cheaper disks
Enable Requester Pays so downloads get higher priority
Issue several byte-range GETs in parallel and join the pieces
Use multipart upload to split the object into parts on the server
versions.explanation: Ranged GETs parallelise downloads (Transfer Acceleration can also help).

versions.question: An instance has SG-A (allows TCP 443 from anywhere) and SG-B (allows TCP 3306 from 10.0.0.0/16). Which inbound traffic is accepted?
options: Both: 443 from anywhere and 3306 from 10.0.0.0/16
Only traffic matching both groups, so effectively nothing
Only 443, because the group listed first takes precedence
Nothing, because rules for different ports conflict across groups
versions.explanation: Rules of all attached groups are merged; a match in any one allows the traffic.

versions.question: How does EC2 evaluate rules when several security groups are attached to one network interface?
options: Groups are checked in attachment order and the first group that matches decides
All rules from every group are merged, and any match allows the traffic
A deny rule in any attached group overrides allows in the other groups
The rule with the lowest number across all attached groups takes priority
versions.explanation: Security groups are allow-only and additive; there is no ordering or deny.

versions.question: An app keeps scratch files on an instance store volume. The instance is stopped and later started. What about the files?
options: They are held encrypted in S3 for seven days after the stop
They are preserved as long as the instance restarts in the same Availability Zone
They are snapshotted to EBS automatically before the stop completes
They are gone, because instance store is temporary storage tied to the host
versions.explanation: Instance store is ephemeral and is wiped on stop or terminate.

versions.question: What is the main risk of relying on an instance store volume for important data?
options: Data vanishes on stop, terminate or host hardware failure, so you replicate it yourself
It is replicated synchronously across three AZs, which adds write latency to every operation
It is billed per GB-month even while the instance is stopped and the disk is empty
It can be attached to only one instance at a time, using Multi-Attach for sharing
versions.explanation: Instance store offers no durability guarantees; backup and replication are on you.

versions.question: Auto Scaling instances need ten minutes to become ready because user data installs lots of packages. What is the best fix?
options: Move the root volume to instance store for quicker package installs
Bake the packages into a golden AMI and keep user data for light final configuration
Increase the user data size limit so more commands run in parallel
Add a cluster placement group so the package downloads travel over a faster, low-latency network
versions.explanation: A pre-built AMI removes install time from boot.

versions.question: Which resource captures OS settings, installed software and agents so new instances launch quickly and identically?
options: A custom Amazon Machine Image
A cluster placement group
A launch template with user data
An EBS snapshot lifecycle policy
versions.explanation: Custom AMIs bake configuration into the image so instances start ready.

versions.question: An RDS instance with unpredictable growth often drops to 5% free storage. The team wants no manual resizing. What should they turn on?
options: Storage autoscaling with a maximum storage limit
Provisioned IOPS so that the volume expands as throughput rises
A nightly Lambda that calls `ModifyDBInstance` with a bigger size
A Multi-AZ DB cluster with two readable standbys
versions.explanation: RDS Storage Auto Scaling grows storage automatically up to the threshold you set.

versions.question: Which condition is part of what triggers RDS storage autoscaling?
options: Free space below 10% of allocated storage for at least 5 minutes
Free space below 25% of allocated storage for at least 1 minute
CPU utilization above 80% across the last three data points
Read IOPS above the provisioned amount for 15 consecutive minutes on the primary
versions.explanation: It also needs 6+ hours since the last storage change, and respects the maximum threshold.

versions.question: An EC2 instance's NFS mount of an EFS file system times out. Which inbound TCP port must the mount target's security group permit?
options: TCP 3260, the iSCSI port
TCP 2049, the NFS port
TCP 873, the rsync port
TCP 445, the SMB port
versions.explanation: EFS uses NFS, which runs on port 2049.

versions.question: What is the recommended source in the EFS mount target's inbound NFS rule?
options: `0.0.0.0/0`, because EFS has no public endpoint anyway
The security group attached to the EC2 instances
The VPC's main network ACL ID
The ARN of the EFS file system
versions.explanation: Referencing the instances' security group keeps access tight even when IPs change.

versions.question: A real-time analytics engine keeps a 2 TB working set entirely in RAM. Which instance category fits?
options: General purpose burstable instances
Accelerated computing with GPUs
Memory optimized, such as the R or X series
Storage optimized with local NVMe
versions.explanation: Large in-memory data sets map to memory-optimized instances.

versions.question: Which instance letters belong to the memory-optimized category?
options: C and the HPC series
R, X and High Memory
I, D and H storage families
T and M burstable types
versions.explanation: Compute is C, storage is I/D/H, general purpose is T/M.

versions.question: An attacker's single IP must be blocked at the subnet edge. Which two facts apply? (Choose two)
options: Network ACLs remember connections, so return traffic needs no rule
Security groups sit at the subnet boundary and process rules in numeric order
Security groups only contain Allow rules, so they cannot block one address
Network ACLs allow explicit Deny rules, evaluated from the lowest rule number
Security groups are stateless and need matching outbound rules for replies
versions.explanation: Only NACLs can deny; SGs are allow-only.

versions.question: Which two statements about statefulness are correct? (Choose two)
options: A network ACL tracks connections and lets responses through on its own
A security group is evaluated per subnet and needs both directions written
Network ACLs attach directly to individual network interfaces
A security group automatically permits replies to traffic it allowed in
A network ACL needs a rule for return traffic, such as ephemeral ports
versions.explanation: SGs are stateful at ENI level; NACLs are stateless at subnet level.

versions.question: In the instance type `c6g.4xlarge`, what does the `6` mean?
options: The count of attached EBS volumes
The hardware generation
The tier of network bandwidth
The number of vCPUs
versions.explanation: Letter = family, number = generation, suffix = size.

versions.question: In `r7i.large`, which part identifies the size within the family?
options: `7i`, generation plus attribute
`large`, the part after the dot
`r7`, family and generation joined
`r`, the instance family letter
versions.explanation: The part after the dot is the size; `r` is family and `7` the generation.

versions.question: The origin needs an `Accept-Language` header and a tracking cookie, but cache hit ratio must not suffer. Where do you list them?
options: In the cache policy, as part of the key
In an Origin Shield setting on the distribution's primary origin
In an origin request policy attached to the behavior
In a field-level encryption profile
versions.explanation: Origin request policies forward extra values without adding them to the cache key.

versions.question: What does a CloudFront origin request policy do?
options: Forwards extra headers, cookies and query strings without adding them to the cache key
Redirects HTTP viewer requests to HTTPS at the edge before they are checked against the cache
Restricts viewers to signed URLs or signed cookies for private content
Defines how long objects stay in the edge cache before they are revalidated
versions.explanation: Cache policy decides the key; origin request policy adds forwarded-only values.

versions.question: Which three names are NOT valid S3 bucket names? (Choose three)
options: Photos_2026
logs.prod.example
data-bucket-s3alias
team-archive
versions.explanation: Uppercase/underscores, IP-address format and the `-s3alias` suffix are not allowed.

versions.question: Pick the two compliant S3 bucket names. (Choose two)
options: ab
xn--cafe-bucket
Reports2026
backup.eu.example
team-archive-01
versions.explanation: Names must be 3-63 chars of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and dots, without `xn--`.

versions.question: Millions of requests against SSE-KMS objects return KMS throttling errors. Which change reduces KMS calls?
options: Turn on S3 versioning
Enable S3 Bucket Keys
Add more prefixes to the bucket
Switch on Transfer Acceleration
versions.explanation: Bucket Keys let S3 reuse a bucket-level key, cutting KMS requests.

versions.question: Why can SSE-KMS throttle at scale when SSE-S3 does not?
options: SSE-KMS objects are capped at 1,000 objects per prefix by the S3 service
A single KMS key serves only one request at a time
Each request triggers a KMS API call counted against the KMS quota
S3 rejects encrypted requests once the bucket policy grows large
versions.explanation: KMS has its own request quotas; SSE-S3 doesn't call KMS.

versions.question: In the CloudFront signed URL flow, who creates the signature and with what?
options: The viewer's browser, signing with the identity of the OAC
The app, signing with a private key whose public key CloudFront holds
CloudFront itself, signing with the KMS key that encrypts the bucket
S3 itself, evaluating a bucket policy condition on each incoming request
versions.explanation: The app signs; CloudFront verifies using the public key.

versions.question: Put these steps for serving private files via CloudFront signed URLs in order.
items: User authenticates with the web app
Backend verifies the user may access the file
Backend creates a signed URL with the private key
Backend sends the signed URL to the browser
Browser requests the URL from CloudFront, which validates the signature with the public key
versions.explanation: The bucket remains private behind OAC; only CloudFront reads it.

versions.question: Lambda functions must reach a database with IAM authentication enforced and no DB password in code. Which design?
options: Add a read replica in a second AZ and point all of the functions' write traffic at it
Put an ElastiCache cluster in front so the app never opens DB connections
Use an RDS Proxy that enforces IAM auth and reads the DB login from Secrets Manager
Limit the database port to the Lambda functions' security group
versions.explanation: RDS Proxy can require IAM auth and holds the real credentials in Secrets Manager.

versions.question: When an RDS Proxy requires IAM authentication, how does the client authenticate?
options: It builds an IAM auth token with the SDK or CLI and uses it as the password
It presents the proxy's security group ID in place of a credential
It sends the database master password inside a custom TLS handshake header field
It supplies the ARN of a Secrets Manager rotation Lambda as the secret
versions.explanation: IAM tokens replace passwords for the client-to-proxy connection.

versions.question: Two instances write to a shared io2 Multi-Attach volume and blocks get overwritten. What is missing?
options: A cluster-aware file system, or coordination of writes in the application
A snapshot lifecycle policy that pauses writes during the backups
An instance store volume that buffers writes on each host
Placing the instances in separate Availability Zones for isolation purposes
versions.explanation: Multi-Attach shares raw blocks; coordination is up to you.

versions.question: Which is a Multi-Attach constraint?
options: The instances must be spread across Regions for durability
It works only with gp3 volumes, not provisioned IOPS ones
It is limited to exactly two attached instances
Attached instances must be in the same AZ as the volume
versions.explanation: Multi-Attach is for io1/io2, same-AZ Nitro instances.

versions.question: Select three situations where a pre-signed S3 URL is the right tool. (Choose three)
options: Granting every IAM role in the account read access
Allowing a mobile app to PUT one photo to a specific key without AWS credentials
Serving a public marketing website
Generating per-user share links on demand
Letting a customer download a private invoice PDF for the next 15 minutes
versions.explanation: Pre-signed URLs give temporary, scoped access to a private object.

versions.question: Which two statements about S3 pre-signed URLs are true? (Choose two)
options: It stays valid forever unless the bucket is deleted
It stops working at expiry or when the signer's credentials expire
The URL carries the permissions of the identity that signed it
Anyone can extend the expiry by editing the query string
versions.explanation: A pre-signed URL inherits the signer's permissions and lifetime limits.

versions.question: A cache policy includes the `Accept-Language` header in the cache key. What happens on a cache miss?
options: The header is stripped before the origin sees the request
It is forwarded only if also listed in an origin request policy
CloudFront forwards the header to the origin with the request
It is sent only when revalidating expired objects
versions.explanation: Values in the cache key are always forwarded.

versions.question: How do a cache policy and an origin request policy relate?
options: Origin request policy values also become part of the cache key
It adds values on top of those already forwarded via the cache key
Values chosen in the cache policy are withheld from the origin server
The two policies must list identical values or the distribution fails
versions.explanation: Origin request policy values are forwarded only, not cached on.

versions.question: Which three settings can a CloudFront cache policy control? (Choose three)
options: Which cookies form the cache key
Which IAM principals may create invalidations
The order of origin failover
Minimum, default and maximum TTL
Which headers form the cache key
versions.explanation: Cache policy: TTLs plus headers, cookies and query strings in the key.

versions.question: Which two can a cache policy configure? (Choose two)
options: A TTL range from 0 seconds up to a year
The TLS ciphers used toward the origin
The custom port of the origin
Which query strings are part of the cache key
versions.explanation: TTLs and key components are cache policy settings.

versions.question: A reporting read replica must survive an AZ outage. Is that configurable?
options: Only if the replica is in another Region
Only for Aurora clusters
No, replicas run in one AZ and must be re-created after an outage
Yes, the replica can itself be deployed as Multi-AZ
versions.explanation: Read replicas can be Multi-AZ for DR.

versions.question: Which statement about RDS read replicas and Multi-AZ is correct?
options: Multi-AZ is available only on the source instance
Enabling Multi-AZ on a replica promotes it to primary automatically
A replica can be Multi-AZ only when it is in another Region
A read replica may itself use Multi-AZ to gain failover protection
versions.explanation: Replicas can be Multi-AZ; this is independent of the source.

versions.question: A NoSQL database needs very high local NVMe IOPS with low latency. Which category?
options: Storage optimized (I, D or H families)
Memory optimized with very large RAM
Compute optimized with high clock speeds
Burstable general purpose instances
versions.explanation: Heavy local storage I/O points to storage optimized.

versions.question: Which instance letters make up the storage-optimized category?
options: I, D and H
R, X and High Memory
T and M
C and HPC
versions.explanation: Storage optimized: I, D, H.

versions.question: How are On-Demand Amazon Linux instances billed?
options: Per hour, with partial hours always rounded up to a full hour
Per minute with a 10-minute minimum
Per second after a 60-second minimum
Per day with a 1-day minimum
versions.explanation: Linux and Windows On-Demand are per-second, one-minute minimum.

versions.question: Which OS is still billed per hour for On-Demand instances?
options: Ubuntu Server
Windows Server
Amazon Linux 2023
SUSE Linux (SLES)
versions.explanation: A few OSes like SUSE remain hourly.

versions.question: A video transcoding batch can pause and resume at any moment. Which purchase option is cheapest?
options: Three-year Reserved Instances
Dedicated Instances for isolation
On-Demand Capacity Reservations
Spot Instances (interruptible)
versions.explanation: Spot is cheapest and suits interruptible work.

versions.question: What is the catch with Spot Instances?
options: Each instance may run for at most one hour
They are offered only in burstable instance families
AWS can reclaim it, with a two-minute warning
They require a one-year upfront payment commitment
versions.explanation: Spot can be interrupted; avoid for critical or stateful jobs.

versions.question: A production server's attached EBS volume needs a snapshot. Is stopping or detaching it mandatory?
options: Only for io2 volumes; gp3 volumes never need it
Yes, the API rejects snapshots of volumes that remain attached
No, though pausing writes or detaching yields a more consistent image
Yes, but only when the volume is encrypted with a KMS key
versions.explanation: Snapshots work on attached volumes; consistency is the only concern.

versions.question: What does a snapshot of an attached, in-use volume capture?
options: It fails unless the volume has first been detached
Only blocks already written, not data still cached in memory
Disk blocks plus the contents of the instance's RAM
Nothing until the instance is stopped, then it starts
versions.explanation: Snapshots are point-in-time copies of written blocks.

versions.question: A hub VPC is peered with two spoke VPCs. Can the spokes reach each other through the hub?
options: No: peering is non-transitive, so peer the spokes or use Transit Gateway
Yes, once the hub route tables list both spoke CIDR ranges in them
Yes, but only when all three VPCs share a Region and account
Only if the hub VPC runs a NAT gateway in each AZ for routing
versions.explanation: Each communicating pair needs its own peering (or a Transit Gateway).

versions.question: Which AWS service lets many VPCs communicate transitively through one hub?
options: Internet gateway
AWS Transit Gateway
NAT gateway
Gateway VPC endpoint
versions.explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional router connecting many VPCs.

versions.question: Which CLI call exchanges an MFA code for temporary credentials?
options: `aws sts get-session-token --serial-number <arn> --token-code <code>`
`aws iam enable-mfa-device`, which registers a new device
`aws iam create-access-key` for the current user
`aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity` using an OIDC token
versions.explanation: get-session-token returns temporary keys after MFA.

versions.question: Arrange the sequence for running AWS CLI commands under MFA protection.
items: Register a virtual or hardware MFA device for the IAM user
Run sts get-session-token with the device serial and the current code
Store the returned access key, secret and session token in a named profile
Run CLI commands with that profile until the credentials expire
versions.explanation: When the session expires, request a new token.

versions.question: Which three statements about Aurora are true? (Choose three)
options: It requires manual storage resizing with downtime
It is a native Oracle-compatible engine
Data is stored as six copies across three AZs
It supports up to 15 read replicas
Storage grows automatically as data increases
versions.explanation: Aurora: 6 copies/3 AZs, auto-growing storage, up to 15 replicas.

versions.question: Which two describe Aurora? (Choose two)
options: Each replica keeps its own separate copy of the data
It offers MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible editions
It is free to self-host
Replica lag is typically under 10 ms because of shared storage
versions.explanation: Replicas share the cluster volume so lag is low.

versions.question: Viewers are almost all in the US and Germany. How can CloudFront cost be reduced?
options: Disable caching to cut edge storage
Block viewers outside the US and Germany with geo restriction
Move to Price Class All for max reach
Restrict it to Price Class 100
versions.explanation: Price Class 100 uses the cheapest edge regions: North America and Europe.

versions.question: What is the trade-off of Price Class 100?
options: Requests from the excluded regions are rejected with an HTTP 403
Viewers outside North America and Europe are served from farther away
HTTPS is unavailable for viewers in the excluded regions
Caching is turned off for every viewer outside the chosen regions
versions.explanation: Cheaper regions only; other viewers get served from further away.

versions.question: A flash sale starts every Monday at 9 AM and capacity must be ready beforehand. Which ASG policy?
options: Target tracking on average request count per target
A rolling instance refresh of the group
A scheduled action that raises desired capacity ahead of time
Simple scaling triggered by a CloudWatch alarm after the spike begins
versions.explanation: Known recurring load means scheduled scaling.

versions.question: Which ASG scaling type forecasts cyclical load from history and pre-provisions capacity?
options: Step scaling
Target tracking
Predictive scaling
Cron-style recurring actions
versions.explanation: Predictive scaling uses ML forecasts.

versions.question: A hotfix to `/index.html` must be live now but the TTL is one day. What do you do?
options: Turn on S3 bucket versioning for the origin
Switch to a different price class
Delete the distribution and create a new one
Create an invalidation for the `/index.html` path
versions.explanation: Invalidation removes the cached copy so the next request fetches the new one.

versions.question: Without an invalidation, when will an edge location fetch the updated file?
options: Once S3 versioning registers a new object version
Right away, when S3 emits a PutObject event
When the object's TTL runs out and the edge revalidates
After the default five-minute refresh window
versions.explanation: Edges serve cached copies until TTL expiry.

versions.question: A company keeps compliance snapshots for seven years, rarely restores them, and can wait days. What reduces cost up to 75%?
options: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore
Put them in the Recycle Bin
Move the snapshots to the archive tier
Turn them into Multi-Attach volumes
versions.explanation: Snapshot Archive is up to 75% cheaper.

versions.question: How long do restores from EBS Snapshot Archive take?
options: Roughly 60 minutes
Between 24 and 72 hours
Within a few minutes
Instantly with Fast Snapshot Restore
versions.explanation: The trade-off for archive storage is slow restore.

versions.question: What is the baseline GET/HEAD request rate per prefix in S3?
options: 1,000 requests per second
5,500 requests per second
10,000 requests per second
3,500 requests per second
versions.explanation: 5,500 GET/HEAD and 3,500 write requests per prefix per second.

versions.question: How can an application exceed the per-prefix request limit?
options: Enable Transfer Acceleration
Spread objects across multiple prefixes
Use larger objects
Open a support ticket to raise the per-prefix limit
versions.explanation: No limit on number of prefixes, so scale by adding prefixes.

versions.question: Name the two operations an S3 Lifecycle rule can apply to objects. (Choose two)
options: Permanently delete objects after a set age
Convert objects to Parquet
Copy objects to another account
Move objects to a colder storage class
versions.explanation: Lifecycle rules transition and expire objects.

versions.question: Logs older than 365 days must be removed automatically. Which lifecycle action type?
options: A replication rule to another bucket
A transition to Glacier Deep Archive
An Object Lock retention period
An expiration action for objects
versions.explanation: Expiration deletes objects; transitions only change class.

versions.question: A Deny policy must trigger when the `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` value is not `aws:kms`. Which condition operator?
options: `StringEquals`
`ForAllValues:StringLike`
`NumericNotEquals`
`StringNotEquals`
versions.explanation: Deny when the header is NOT aws:kms.

versions.question: Which condition key holds the encryption header value sent with a PutObject request?
options: `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption`
`aws:SecureTransport`
`s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`
`s3:x-amz-storage-class`
versions.explanation: That key reflects the SSE header.

versions.question: Default encryption alone does not stop a client explicitly asking for AES256. Which two steps enforce SSE-KMS? (Choose two)
options: Make SSE-KMS the bucket's default encryption setting
Enable Object Lock in compliance mode
Turn on Transfer Acceleration
Add a bucket policy Deny on PutObject when the header isn't aws:kms
versions.explanation: Default covers headerless uploads; the Deny rejects others.

versions.question: Which two statements about default encryption and a bucket policy are true? (Choose two)
options: Default encryption overrides whatever header the client sends
Default encryption applies only to uploads that specify no encryption
A Deny on the header rejects requests that explicitly specify another method
A bucket policy runs after default encryption so it cannot reject
versions.explanation: Bucket policies are evaluated before default encryption.

versions.question: From which three sources can you pick an image when launching an instance? (Choose three)
options: An EBS snapshot ID used directly as boot source
Vendor images subscribed via AWS Marketplace
AWS-provided public AMIs
An ISO file in an S3 bucket
AMIs created in your own account
versions.explanation: Public, own and Marketplace AMIs.

versions.question: Which two can be used as an AMI source? (Choose two)
options: A custom AMI baked from an existing instance
An EBS snapshot launched directly without registering an image
An Elastic IP address
A Marketplace AMI from a vendor
versions.explanation: Snapshots must be registered as an AMI first.

versions.question: A branch office needs an encrypted tunnel to a VPC by tomorrow, with no dedicated circuit. What fits?
options: IPsec tunnels through a virtual private gateway
VPC peering between the VPC and the office network
AWS PrivateLink endpoint service to the office
A dedicated 1 Gbps circuit ordered via Direct Connect
versions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN sets up in minutes over the internet, encrypted.

versions.question: Which statement compares Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect correctly?
options: Direct Connect rides the public internet while VPN uses a private circuit
VPN needs a physical cross-connect in a colocation facility, DX does not
Both can be provisioned within minutes and both encrypt traffic by default
VPN is ready in minutes and encrypted; Direct Connect is slower and not encrypted by default
versions.explanation: VPN: fast, encrypted, internet; DX: dedicated, slower to provision.

versions.question: Which move can an S3 Lifecycle rule NOT perform?
options: Standard to Intelligent-Tiering
Glacier Flexible Retrieval to Deep Archive
One Zone-IA to Glacier Flexible Retrieval
Standard-IA back up to S3 Standard
versions.explanation: Transitions go toward colder classes only.

versions.question: What direction do lifecycle transitions follow?
options: In either direction between any two classes, as configured
Only from colder classes up to warmer ones
Only between classes that use the same retrieval fee model
Only toward colder, cheaper classes; going back up requires copying
versions.explanation: Lifecycle waterfall is one-way.

versions.question: A teammate logs in over SSH as `ec2-user`. Which AMI family is the instance most likely running?
options: Windows Server
Debian
Amazon Linux
Ubuntu Server
versions.explanation: Amazon Linux defaults to ec2-user.

versions.question: Which pairing of AMI and default SSH login user is correct?
options: Amazon Linux uses `admin`; Ubuntu uses `ec2-user`
Amazon Linux uses `ubuntu`; Ubuntu uses `root`
Amazon Linux uses `ec2-user`; Ubuntu uses `ubuntu`
Both use `ec2-user`, differing only by key pair
versions.explanation: Wrong user gives Permission denied (publickey).

versions.question: A streaming company wants cached copies of videos physically near viewers in many cities. Which AWS infrastructure delivers this?
options: Extra AZs in the home Region
Availability Zones in the home Region
Additional AWS Regions
CloudFront points of presence
versions.explanation: Edge locations serve cached content near users.

versions.question: Which statement about edge locations is true?
options: Many are spread across cities worldwide to serve cached content
Customers launch EC2 instances in them like Availability Zones
They hold the primary copies of RDS storage volumes
There is exactly one per Region, mirroring the AZ count
versions.explanation: Edge locations are CDN points of presence.

versions.question: Which three can be registered in an ALB target group? (Choose three)
options: Private IP addresses reachable in a VPC or on premises
Instance IDs
An S3 static website endpoint
A serverless function running on Lambda
A CloudFront distribution
versions.explanation: ALB targets: instances, IPs, Lambda.

versions.question: Which two can be ALB targets? (Choose two)
options: An S3 bucket
An EC2 Auto Scaling group
A DynamoDB table
A serverless function running on Lambda
versions.explanation: ALB targets EC2/ASG, IPs and Lambda.
